cohort_selection_rule: All non-ablated runs in artifacts/ whose backend is one of groq/qwen/qwen3.8-27b, groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b, groq/openai/gpt-oss-20b, groq/qwen/qwen3.6-27b (the four Groq-hosted models named in the 'Current recommendation' and 'Known provider limits' sections of MODEL_COMPARISON.md), on one of the six live-dev-* text fixtures that back the per-scenario matrix: development-text-correction-01, device-correction-before-plan, lost-response-status-reconciliation, support-read-then-service, stale-read-after-correction, stale-read-after-device-correction. Audio and vision live-dev fixtures (live-dev-audio-correction-01, live-dev-frame-device-panel-01) are excluded: that evidence belongs to the separate audio/vision E2E slice this task must not touch. Local (Ollama/NVIDIA) models are excluded: they are documented separately in LOCAL_MODEL_2026-09-13.md and INFERENCE_TUNING_2026-09-14.md and run on different hardware.

sanitization.issue: 16 traces were reported by the orchestrator to contain the Groq organization id in reasoner_evidence.requests[].error_detail (raw provider error bodies from the pre-R5 diagnostics path). An independent repo-wide grep for the pattern org_[0-9a-zA-Z]{10,}, excluding .git and .venv, found the identifier in 13 files under artifacts/ (11 *.jsonl run traces and 2 report.json summaries), all sharing the same single organization id value (not reproduced here). No API keys or bearer tokens were found in any file considered for this bundle.
sanitization.action: Sanitised, not excluded. Every copied trace passes through a regex substitution (org_[0-9a-zA-Z]{10,} -> [REDACTED_ORG_ID]) applied to every JSON line, not only the known-contaminated ones, as defence in depth. All 11 contaminated *.jsonl runs fall inside this cohort and are included, sanitised, because they are genuine 429 admission-control failures relevant to attempted-run reliability (see eligibility 'infra_admission_failure'). The 2 contaminated report.json files are hand-written summaries, not run_metadata traces the scoreboard reads; they were not copied into this bundle and were not modified in artifacts/.

known_gaps: source_sha256 (and thus 'commit and source hash' in this manifest) covers only *.py files under src/accessflow/. It does not cover scripts/, the dependency lockfile/pyproject.toml, scenario JSON content beyond scenario_sha256, or environment/.env settings. A clean-clone run reproduces the *scoreboard table* from these traces; it does not re-prove the original model behaviour, since these are hosted-API calls that cannot be replayed offline.

53 of these 57 runs predate run_id/run_started_at/run_ended_at (those fields were added partway through this cohort's collection) and fall back to file mtime for ordering, marked accordingly wherever shown; mtime is not a verified chronology. The remaining 4 (r1-live/qwen-device.jsonl, r1-live/qwen-support.jsonl, r2-live/qwen-reconcile.jsonl, r3-live/device.jsonl) do carry a recorded run_id and UTC start/end time. The bundle build step copies each source file's original mtime onto its sanitised copy (os.utime) specifically so the mtime-fallback signal is not further destroyed by the copy itself; it is still only the original developer's machine clock, not a verified run timestamp, for the 53 runs that rely on it.
declared_hardware for Groq-hosted runs describes the requesting client machine, not Groq's serving hardware, which is not disclosed by the provider.
